answers.question: 144 Q1 · Signing off a milestone means running every test in the repo (~11,600). Run one at a time, that takes ~1¾ h and often hits the 2 h kill. Split across 16 parallel processes, it took 24 min on a quiet machine and 60 min today with other work running. Your story says sign-off should take "minutes". What's the longest you'll accept?
answers.answer: No more than 15mins. There's a work item to optimize

answers.question: 144 Q2 · When the machine is busy, some tests fail and then pass when re-run on their own (13 did today); they are timing flakes, not real bugs. The run already re-runs every failure on its own. When a test only passes on the re-run, should sign-off still pass?
answers.answer: These are shit tests, not properly isolated. These need to be logged

answers.question: 144 Q3 · `aof work regression-gate`, the command that records a milestone's sign-off, still runs the tests one at a time. So 131, 133 and 142 were all accepted with a written override that pointed at a separate parallel run instead. Should the sign-off command itself run the tests in parallel?
answers.answer: We should be able to pass in settings

answers.question: 144 Q4 · Even in parallel, the run can't finish before its slowest test file does. Three files hold ~1¾ h of the 10¾ h total: loop-command-wave (61 min, 49 tests), loop-command-reconcile (25 min) and work-dispatch-lanes (23 min). Your story's title includes "the slow tail trimmed". Should speeding these up be part of this story?
answers.answer: Why are you asking all these testing questions? What does this have to do with milestone 134? It's not your fucking job to fix all the tests
